quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing without flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks right away and as fast as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to let any train pass first.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to let any train pass first.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to let trains pass before you cross railroad tracks. Wait until your whole vehicle can fit on the other side before crossing. Do not change gears while crossing because your vehicle could stall.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to create more space between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to spot tailgaters or fast-approaching cars. If someone is following too close, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Alcohol is the single greatest common factor in fatal car crashes.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the number one killer on American roads. It harms your vision and slows your reaction time. Even small amounts of alcohol affect your driving, even if you are not legally drunk.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are not in the right lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and back up to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn at an intersection, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: Orange signs are:

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mark work zones on highways. These signs are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols. They warn you that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line when:

options.text: Doing so would interfere with traffic.
Turning left into a driveway.
The car in front of you has broken down.
Passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do it safely without getting in the way of other traffic.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a steady green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.
Construction workers are on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a pedestrian crossing is coming. Drive carefully and be alert for people crossing the road.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is beginning.
You may see more pedestrians ahead.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: School zone speed limits apply only during certain times. An "End school zone" sign tells you that the lower speed limit zone is over.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Not use any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on cloudy days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming car or within 500 feet of a car ahead of you. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from a ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you have space to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are permitted on the upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is open to one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead is wide enough for only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the upcoming bridge may be too narrow to safely meet or pass a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver should continue driving without stopping.
One driver should wave the other drivers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first.
questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all drivers must stop. The first to arrive goes first. If two arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes and encounter a bicyclist ahead. How should you safely pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
Continue driving straight. The bicyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist as you would any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on regular roads, or 5 feet on higher speed roads or when passing multiple bicyclists. Do not honk, as it may startle them and cause a crash.

questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the streets.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You must drive with extreme caution where children are present. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A no passing zone.
A one-way traffic area.
The blind spot of a large vehicle.
An area for motor vehicles only.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are the large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Avoid staying in these areas.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both driving too slowly on certain highways and speeding can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both driving too slowly on certain highways and speeding can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 mph, survival is almost impossible. Driving slower than traffic can also be dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to make sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to make sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and check behind your car before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are near. This is the safest way to back up.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to make others aware of you.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without making an emergency stop. This helps prevent the driver behind you from crashing into you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Curve.
Turn right or left.
Traffic can only go in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic can only go in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A one-way sign tells you that traffic only moves in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line on your side, you may pass if:

options.text: Only in an emergency.
You are on an expressway.
The road ahead is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: When you have a broken yellow line on your side and a solid line on the other side, you may pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as you.
If the pedestrian signals you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or crossing unsafely.

questions.question: When a curb is painted ____, it shows a handicap parking space.

options.text: Yellow
Blue
White
Green

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue
questions.explanation: A blue painted curb marks a handicap parking space. Only people with a handicap license plate or tag may park there.

questions.question: If you need to drive in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Never drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. You must use headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian knows your vehicle is there.
Always give the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Only give the right-of-way when the pedestrian has it.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can safely be held by a strong adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not get hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand up in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand up in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats. No one can safely hold a child during a crash or sudden stop. Always keep children properly fastened in a seat.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Signal for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens. Drive to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, clear it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren nearby but do not know where the vehicle is, safely pull over to the right and stop until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn you about hazards ahead.

questions.question: Which of these is used on some highways to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows show which lanes to use for specific actions, like driving straight or turning.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use your parking lights only.
Use your headlights only.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights. This helps other drivers see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as:

options.text: A solid red light.
A stop sign.
A yield sign.
A caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing light means stop completely. Proceed only when it is safe. A stop sign may also be posted at this location.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:

options.text: Flat.
Curvy.
In the sun.
Shaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas under trees or buildings freeze faster than other parts of the road. They are also the last areas to dry out.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Excessive stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Excessive speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Excessive speed.
questions.explanation: At high speeds, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and the vehicle slides on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to check for passing vehicles. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians walking against the traffic light.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing against the light. Pedestrians may misjudge the signal.

questions.question: This green arrow on a lane control signal means:

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down means you can use that lane.

questions.question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not working due to a power outage, what should you do?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you will do.
Turn on your hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat it like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers and proceed when it is your turn and safe to do so.

questions.question: If a police officer thinks you are driving under the influence, can you refuse a test?

options.text: Yes, you can always refuse.
Yes, you can refuse if it is your first offense.
No, you cannot refuse.
Yes, you can take the test later.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you cannot refuse.
questions.explanation: If an officer suspects you are driving under the influence, you must take a blood, breath, or urine test. Refusing the test will result in your license being revoked.

questions.question: After you stop for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you before moving.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking on the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: To be ready for anything on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and both sides of the road.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake while driving.
Focus only on the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and both sides of the road.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous situations depends on spotting problems early. Looking far ahead does not mean staring at the center of the road. You need to look at the entire road, including both sides.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: The driver
Child passengers
Adult passengers
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: In Nevada, everyone in a moving vehicle must wear a seat belt. Children under 6 years old and those under 60 pounds must sit in an approved child safety seat.

questions.question: You should use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: The person is deaf.
The person is a police officer.
The person is blind.
The person has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The person is blind.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and yield the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to prevent injury to the pedestrian.

questions.question: You should leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopping:

options.text: On a hill.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when stopped on an uphill slope. If the vehicle in front rolls backward when traffic starts, there is less chance of a collision.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be prepared to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop at a yield sign if traffic requires it.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:

options.text: Planning extra travel time.
Following posted speed limits.
Using turn signals correctly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: As more drivers use the roads, road rage increases. To prevent road rage, use turn signals, follow speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: Drivers may text while driving:

options.text: Never.
Anytime.
If they are a very skilled driver.
If they only look away from the road for a moment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone or other handheld device while driving is not allowed, unless using a hands-free option. Texting or reading messages on any device while driving is against the law.

questions.question: Drivers may always make U-turns in school zones.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Nevada law does not allow U-turns in school zones unless there are no children present, the school is closed, or signs show that school restrictions are not in effect.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two-way traffic is ahead.
